title: refactor(plugins): one authority each for AggregationConfig, ConditionalFormattingRule and ViewType (objectui#6349, batch 7)
body:
Refs #6349 (batch 7)

Clause-②: yes

Batch 7 of the one-authority burn-down, on claim `6088763852` (seat `domain:ui#3`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`). Three "plugin vs `@object-ui/types`" rows of `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` converge, so the ledger goes from 19 rows to 16. Each row was two meanings behind one name. In all three, `@object-ui/types` keeps the general name and the plugin side gives up the name. Types and comments only: no runtime behaviour changes, and no emitted JavaScript changes.

This PR has no closing keyword. The card stays open for later batches.

## What each row was (measured on base `e391f876`)

The member lists below come from one TypeScript program over each package's BUILT root entry (`exports["."].types`), with dist rebuilt for the base tree.

**`AggregationConfig`: two meanings, so the plugin side is renamed.**

| site | members | meaning | built entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/data-protocol.ts` | `function` (8 arms, incl. `array_agg` and `string_agg`), `field?`, `alias?`, `distinct?`, `separator?` | a query-AST aggregation: `DriverQueryConfig.aggregations`, compiled by `@object-ui/core`'s `QueryASTBuilder` | exported at the types root and read through it by core's `query-ast.ts` |
| `packages/plugin-grid/src/useGroupedData.ts` | `field`, `type` (`AggregationType`, 6 arms) | one per-group aggregation drawn in a group header (`ObjectGridSchema.aggregations`) | exported at the plugin-grid root; 0 readers through it in the repo, and 0 hits in `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 |

The two share only `field`, and even that differs (`field?` against `field`). A re-point would retype the grid's `type` key as `function`, which the grid's runtime reads, so it is not a types-only move. The grid's declaration is the narrower meaning. It becomes `GroupAggregationConfig`, and the plugin-grid root publishes that name in place of `AggregationConfig`. The members are unchanged.

**`ConditionalFormattingRule`: the plugin side was an alias of a name that already exists.** The kanban site was `export type ConditionalFormattingRule = KanbanConditionalFormattingRule` in `KanbanImpl.tsx`. `@object-ui/types` declares both `ConditionalFormattingRule` (the `object-grid` and `list-view` rule) and `KanbanConditionalFormattingRule` (the `object-kanban` rule). They differ by one member: the grid's rule carries the retired `expression?: never` tombstone, and the kanban rule does not. So the alias put the kanban meaning behind the grid's name. The kanban meaning already has its specific name, so the alias is deleted and the board spells `KanbanConditionalFormattingRule`. The alias had 0 importers. No package entry reaches `KanbanImpl.d.ts`: a program rooted at the plugin-kanban entry loads 7 of the package's own declaration files, and `KanbanImpl.d.ts` is not one of them. So the alias published nothing.

**`ViewType`: two unions, so the plugin side's alias is deleted.** `@object-ui/types`' `ViewType` has 11 members: the spec's list-view types plus the `list` and `detail` categories. plugin-list's `ViewType` was an alias of `@object-ui/core`'s `ListViewVisualization`, which has 9 members: the same set without `list` and `detail`. The switcher's two total maps (icons and labels) are keyed on the 9-member union. A re-point to the 11-member union would make both maps incomplete, which is a compile error. Filling that gap would need icons and labels for `list` and `detail`, which is a runtime change. The narrower meaning already has its own name, so the alias is deleted. `ViewSwitcher.tsx` and `ListView.tsx` spell `ListViewVisualization`, and the plugin-list root no longer publishes a `ViewType`. It had 0 readers through that entry in the repo (control: the same scan of import clauses finds 23 other bindings from that root, `ListView` ×21 among them), and `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 has 0 hits.

**Why no re-point anywhere.** Batch 3's rule makes `@object-ui/types` the only legal authority. In each row the plugin side means something narrower than the `types` name, and both meanings are live. So the rule of batches 4 to 6 applies: rename the narrower side, and keep the general name on `types`. Where the narrower side was only an alias of a name that already exists, the alias goes, and no new name is coined.

## Published surface, base vs head

This is one TypeScript program per tree over each package's built root entry. Dist was rebuilt for each tree, and every head marker was read in dist before measuring.

- **Exported name sets:**
  - types 708 = 708; core 513 = 513; plugin-kanban 25 = 25; plugin-view 39 = 39;
  - plugin-grid 50 = 50: `AggregationConfig` out, `GroupAggregationConfig` in, with identical members;
  - plugin-list 20 to 19: `ViewType` out.
- **Unchanged shapes:** types' `AggregationConfig`, `ConditionalFormattingRule`, `KanbanConditionalFormattingRule` and `ViewType` (11 members); core's `ListViewVisualization` (9 members); plugin-list's `ViewSwitcherProps`, whose members are still typed on `ListViewVisualization`.
- **An external consumer**, probed as a virtual file that resolves the packages through `node_modules`:
  - the base spelling `import type { AggregationConfig } from '@object-ui/plugin-grid'` fails loudly at head with TS2724, which names the replacement: "Did you mean 'GroupAggregationConfig'?";
  - `import type { ViewType } from '@object-ui/plugin-list'` fails with TS2305;
  - the migration targets compile at head (`GroupAggregationConfig`; `ListViewVisualization` from `@object-ui/core`; `ViewSwitcherProps['currentView']`): 0 diagnostics;
  - the control leg is the four general names imported from `@object-ui/types`. It reads 0 diagnostics on base and on head;
  - on base, the old spellings read 0 diagnostics, and the new grid name reads TS2724, so the probe is lit.
- **Emitted output:** base and head dist differ only in declaration files and their maps:
  - plugin-grid: `index`, `useGroupedData`, `useServerGrouping`;
  - plugin-kanban: `KanbanImpl`;
  - plugin-list: `index`, `ListView`, `ViewSwitcher`.

  No `.js` file differs in any of the six packages, and types, core and plugin-view dist are byte-identical. So no first-load bytes move.

## Changesets

| file | grade | why |
|---|---|---|
| `6349-batch7-plugin-grid.md` | `minor` | A published name leaves the root (`AggregationConfig`) and its replacement arrives (`GroupAggregationConfig`). Breaking-change note with the migration. |
| `6349-batch7-plugin-list.md` | `minor` | A published name leaves the root (`ViewType`). Breaking-change note naming `ListViewVisualization` from `@object-ui/core`. |
| `6349-batch7-plugin-kanban.md` | `patch` | A module-local alias no entry reached. Nothing published moves. |

`@object-ui/types` is not touched, so it gets no changeset. The grades follow the claim's per-package criterion. ⛔ No `major`.

## Docs

`packages/plugin-grid/README.md` lists the package's type exports, and it now names `GroupAggregationConfig`. `check:readme-exports` proves the edit was needed: when the base README is fed against head dist (`--readme` override), it flags `AggregationConfig` at that line as `wrong-path`, owned by `@object-ui/types`. No README or docs page names plugin-list's `ViewType` or the kanban alias.

## Gates

All gates were read at head `ceb7b297f`. Heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock`.

- The gate, `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts`: exit 0, `Tests 11 passed (11)`. The ledger has 16 rows.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/plugin-kanban/`, `packages/plugin-list/` and 31 test files elsewhere that read a touched file's text or path (types, core, app-shell, the console, i18n, react, sdui-parser, calendar, gantt, map, view and scripts): exit 0, `Test Files 223 passed (223)`, `Tests 3076 passed (3076)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-grid/`: exit 0, `Test Files 197 passed (197)`, `Tests 1851 passed (1851)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/PKG type-check` for plugin-grid, plugin-kanban, plugin-list, plugin-view, core and types, with dist rebuilt and the script names echoed: one chained run, exit 0, 0 `error TS` lines.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts`: exit 0.
- `check:doc-snippets`: 785 of 785 blocks judged, 0 failed. It ran after its own scoped build.
- `check:readme-exports`: OK, with 582 of 582 self-imports real.
- Other gates, each exit 0:
  - `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `check:icon-record-names` (it anchors on the plugin-list switcher's `VIEW_ICONS`), `check:spec-symbols` and `check:handler-key-reads`;
  - `check:new-line-citations`, which reports 0 new;
  - `check-changeset-no-major`;
  - `check-changeset-presence`, which reads 7 source files of 3 released packages and 3 changesets.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 8 touched TS files: 0 errors. Two warnings fall on changed lines in `ListView.tsx`, and both are the same rule on the same construct at base (`no-explicit-any` on a filter callback, `set-state-in-effect`). Those lines changed only their type name. The file has 187 warnings at base and 187 at head.
- The governed-queue guard reads NOT GOVERNED over 12 paths.
- `git merge-tree` against `main` `e391f876` is clean.

Not run locally:
- **The full app-shell suite.** CI runs it. app-shell names none of these three types, and it reads the touched packages only through dist whose JS is byte-identical.
- **The type-checks of app-shell, the console and the other dependants of these plugins.** No file outside the three plugins names a removed or renamed export (a repo-wide grep), and every other published shape is unchanged.
- **The i18n gates.** No locale pack changed.

## Reverse verification

Every leg went through `ablation-replace` in wrap mode. The predictions were written before any leg ran. Each leg landed on disk: the anchor count went from 1 to 0, the replacement count from 0 to 1, and the blob changed. Each was restored with blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, which the tool checked and the driver checked again. The gate is a source scan, so no dist leg applies.

| leg | mutation | result (as predicted) |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | the `AggregationConfig` row put back | `Tests 1 failed / 10 passed`; `no longer collides at:` lists `useGroupedData.ts` and `data-protocol.ts` |
| S2 | the `ConditionalFormattingRule` row put back | same verdict; lists `KanbanImpl.tsx` and `objectql.ts` |
| S3 | the `ViewType` row put back | same verdict; lists `ViewSwitcher.tsx` and `views.ts` |
| F1 | the plugin-grid barrel aliases `GroupAggregationConfig as AggregationConfig` (the tempting back-compat shim) | `AggregationConfig — a NEW colliding name`: the plugin-grid barrel (aliasing re-export) and `data-protocol.ts` (interface declaration) |
| F2 | `KanbanImpl.tsx` re-declares the alias | `ConditionalFormattingRule — a NEW colliding name`: `KanbanImpl.tsx` (type declaration) and `objectql.ts` (interface declaration) |
| F3 | the plugin-list barrel publishes `ListViewVisualization as ViewType` | `ViewType — a NEW colliding name`: the plugin-list barrel (aliasing re-export) and `views.ts` (type declaration) |
| control | unmutated | `Tests 11 passed (11)` |

## Acceptance notes

- **One new published name.** `GroupAggregationConfig` is new on the plugin-grid root. It is the rename target the claim's rule implies for a published site, so this PR does not treat it as an extra export. If the seat reads it otherwise, the claim needs an amendment for it.
- **No replacement export on plugin-list.** The root drops `ViewType` and does not re-export `ListViewVisualization`. That name is already published at the `@object-ui/core` root, and a second export site would add nothing. `ViewSwitcherProps['currentView']` names the same union from this package.
- **Gate prose.** Two prose lines in the gate file described `ConditionalFormattingRule` as "the contested name". They now say "the bare name", because it is no longer contested. The near-spelling fixtures themselves are unchanged.
- **JSDoc on the changed sites.** `GroupAggregationConfig`, the kanban comment and the switcher comment each say why the general name is not used, so the next author does not restore it.
- **The grid shape is still declared twice, unnamed.** `GroupAggregationConfig` has the same members as the inline element type of `ObjectGridSchema.aggregations` in `@object-ui/types` (and its zod twin). That is a structural copy, not a name collision under the gate. It is noted here and not filed.
